en.title: Minimum Moves of Characters to the End to Get the Reversed String
en.description:
Each time, remove one character from any position of the binary string and append it to the end. The target is the reverse of the original string. Find the minimum number of operations.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: One line containing a binary string. The original bounds are 1≤length≤100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 3; 1; and 0, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Let the target be the reverse of the original string. Scan the original string and greedily match the longest possible prefix of the target, starting from its beginning; the answer is the number of unmatched characters.
